scenes.tts: Did stretch cause these cells to divide, or did the experiment only make more cells glow green? And how many experiments are hidden inside one dish? Watch one bench before any results appear.
scenes.visual: Hook first on a dark 16:9 frame. A large grey culture dish fills the centre. Blue epithelial-cell cartoons drift gently inside; several nuclei turn green while gold question marks orbit the dish. White stretch arrows pull the dish sideways. A counter rapidly reaches 600 cells, then folds into one outlined dish. Keep all labels at least 34 px. Label the cell-state cartoon 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Did stretch cause these cells to divide, or did the experiment only make more cells glow green? And how many experiments are hidden inside one dish? Watch one bench before any results appear.

scenes.visual: Keep the same bench and dish dimly visible. Bring in the title 'Before the Data Arrive' above three empty gold-edged slots labelled 'prediction', 'endpoint', and 'independent unit'. The title settles, then fades while the three slots remain.

scenes.tts: Place two competing models beside the dish. Model A says stretch is enough for division. Model B says stretch starts the cycle, but another signal is needed for completion. Both predict more green cells. The green snapshot cannot choose between them.
scenes.visual: On the carried bench, slide in two large cards from opposite sides. Card A shows a schematic red cell becoming green and then two gold daughter cells. Card B shows red becoming green, pausing at a grey barrier, then reaching daughters only after a second gold signal block arrives. Animate both green stages together; leave the completion rows visibly different.
scenes.narration: Place two competing models beside the dish. Model A says stretch is enough for division. Model B says stretch starts the cycle, but another signal is needed for completion. Both predict more green cells. The green snapshot cannot choose between them.

scenes.tts: A useful prediction sits where the models disagree. A shared prediction cannot test the choice. Here, the disagreement is completed division. The first gold lock closes: write each model's numerical prediction before collecting an image.
scenes.visual: Move both model cards into a two-row comparison grid attached to the bench. The shared 'green cells' row fades to grey. The different 'completed division' row expands to fill most of the frame. A gold key marked 'different result' turns inside the prediction slot, which closes like a lock. Numbers remain blank boxes because this scene establishes the choice, not values.
scenes.narration: A useful prediction sits where the models disagree. A shared prediction cannot test the choice. Here, the disagreement is completed division. The first gold lock closes: write each model's numerical prediction before collecting an image.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Both paths are real observations, but only one separates these models. Is it more green cells now, or more tracked divisions later? Hold your answer while the two paths move.
scenes.visual: Return one large schematic cell path to centre. It branches after the green cell. The upper branch stops at a green snapshot camera. The lower branch continues toward a gold two-daughter icon. A bright question stays above both branches. Cells pulse slowly; do not reveal a check mark.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Both paths are real observations, but only one separates these models. Is it more green cells now, or more tracked divisions later? Hold your answer while the two paths move.

scenes.visual: Hold the complete prediction frame. Keep the green nucleus pulsing and the tracking arrow creeping slowly toward the two-daughter icon. The question remains fully visible; no answer highlight appears during the pause.

scenes.tts: Fucci is a two-color cell-cycle reporter. In its simplest picture, green marks entry into S phase, not completion of the cycle. The camera must follow one cell's identity across time. Follow that cell until it becomes two daughters. For division claims, track cells to division instead of counting green cells.
scenes.visual: The snapshot branch shrinks and receives the label 'S-phase entry'. On the carried lower branch, animate one red cell turning green, rounding, then separating into two dim daughter cartoons outlined in gold that slowly turn red. The gold tracking line stays attached to the same cell identity. The endpoint slot closes around the label 'observed division'. Mark the lifecycle strip 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Fucci is a two-color cell-cycle reporter. In its simplest picture, green marks entry into S phase, not completion of the cycle. The camera must follow one cell's identity across time. Follow that cell until it becomes two daughters. For division claims, track cells to division instead of counting green cells.

scenes.tts: Next, ask what received treatment independently. Every cell here shared one dish, one pipetting, and one stretch. If the dish is odd, every cell carries that oddity. When treatment is applied to a whole dish, the dish is the experimental unit.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the central dish. Blue cell dots move together as a pipette adds a teal treatment drop and stretch arrows pull the whole dish. Thin lines connect every cell to one blue dish outline. The 600-cell counter collapses again into one large dish token, which slides into the independent-unit slot and closes it.
scenes.narration: Next, ask what received treatment independently. Every cell here shared one dish, one pipetting, and one stretch. If the dish is odd, every cell carries that oddity. When treatment is applied to a whole dish, the dish is the experimental unit.

scenes.tts: Measuring more cells describes that dish more precisely, but it does not repeat treatment. Fresh runs do. A new day with new dishes can expose run-to-run variation. Three separately treated dish pairs give three independent summaries per condition.
scenes.visual: The single bench stretches into three day columns colored teal, purple, and orange. In each column, one control dish and one treated dish receive separate pipette drops. Hundreds of small blue dots compress into one large run-summary symbol per dish. A label changes from '3 dishes x 200 cells' to '3 run summaries per condition'.
scenes.narration: Measuring more cells describes that dish more precisely, but it does not repeat treatment. Fresh runs do. A new day with new dishes can expose run-to-run variation. Three separately treated dish pairs give three independent summaries per condition.

scenes.tts: A SuperPlot keeps both levels visible. Small dots show cells, while large symbols show run summaries. Run two now stands out instead of disappearing in the pool. A SuperPlot keeps cell variation visible while comparing independent runs.
scenes.visual: Transform the three paired dish columns into the lesson's computed SuperPlot. Plot each cell as a small dot in a strip above 100% for EdU-positive or below 0% for EdU-negative, colored by run. Place large run-mean symbols at 20/34, 25/27, and 15/28 percent EdU-positive. Join each control mean to its treated mean. Run two's line is nearly flat while runs one and three rise. Axes read 'control', 'treated', and 'percent EdU-positive'.
scenes.narration: A SuperPlot keeps both levels visible. Small dots show cells, while large symbols show run summaries. Run two now stands out instead of disappearing in the pool. A SuperPlot keeps cell variation visible while comparing independent runs.

scenes.tts: The three locks now align. In shared-dish cell experiments, lock the prediction, endpoint and independent unit before the data arrive. Break one link, and the conclusion changes meaning. With all three aligned, the claim, measurement and analysis answer the same question. Controls then test whether a dull explanation could produce that answer.
scenes.visual: Transform the SuperPlot back into the bench. The three closed gold slots form a horizontal chain above the dish: prediction shows different model outcomes; endpoint shows tracked daughters; independent unit shows three dish summaries. A gold line travels through all three and lights a final white claim card. Keep gentle cell motion in the dish.
scenes.narration: The three locks now align. In shared-dish cell experiments, lock the prediction, endpoint and independent unit before the data arrive. Break one link, and the conclusion changes meaning. With all three aligned, the claim, measurement and analysis answer the same question. Controls then test whether a dull explanation could produce that answer.

scenes.tts: Return to the opening dish. Six hundred glowing cells can be valuable observations. They are still one treated unit, and green still marks S-phase entry. More dots cannot repair a mismatched endpoint. Trust the conclusion only when all three locks fit.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the opening dish at full height. The 600 blue and green cells remain visible, but a blue bracket encloses the dish as one unit. A gold tracked path reaches two daughters beside it. The three lock icons settle above the dish, and the original question marks transform into check marks only when all locks are present.
scenes.narration: Return to the opening dish. Six hundred glowing cells can be valuable observations. They are still one treated unit, and green still marks S-phase entry. More dots cannot repair a mismatched endpoint. Trust the conclusion only when all three locks fit.

scenes.visual: End card on the dark ground with the site's mascot waving above the line 'Lock prediction, endpoint, and independent unit before the data.' Keep the line in high-contrast white, centred, and 12 words or fewer.
